title: AI Self-preferencing in Algorithmic Hiring: Empirical Evidence and Insights

live_model.evidence: "we generate multiple counterfactual versions using...GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4-turbo..."; Figure ("GPT-4-turbo / GPT-4o-mini / GPT-4o / 93.0%").

prompt.location: Appendix B (resume-generation prompt and evaluator/judge prompt)
prompt.note: One prompt rewrites a human resume into an LLM-authored version; a separate evaluator prompt asks a judge LLM to pick the higher-quality resume.

claim.metric: LLM-vs-Human statistical-parity self-preference bias (%) for GPT-4-turbo-generated resumes
claim.location: Figure ("LLM-vs-Human Statistical Parity Self-preference Bias"), GPT-4-turbo bar
claim.judge: llm:gpt-4o (and separately DeepSeek-V3, LLaMA-3.3-70B, as the three evaluator models)

data.source: publicly available dataset of 2,484 anonymized human-written resumes (a separate count of 2,245 also appears in the paper, likely a filtered subset)

notes: GPT-4-turbo is one of 3 closed-source generator models (plus 4 open-source) whose resumes are judged; the exact chart-to-text mapping of the 93.0%/91.2% bars to GPT-4-turbo specifically is inferred from consistent label ordering across two figures, not a literal inline sentence value.
